data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 claims the centralized service is more resilient by eliminating dependency density, but its own countercondition admits the centralized control plane can suffer catastrophic failure and that internal redundancy may share a single fate-sharing domain. These are precisely the correlated failure modes the problem highlights: a unified control plane is itself a shared cause whose failure can trigger correlated collapse across all redundant components. The claim asserts superior resilience while conceding the exact failure class that refutes it. A single large service with a global control plane has a correlated single point of failure that a decentralized network lacks, so the unqualified claim is not supported.
